songs.title: Razor Bloom - Overdrive
songs.description: The angular C-minor hook returns on gnarly overdrive guitar, with a snarling synth-bass answer and tightly broken drum-and-bass kicks. Listen for the charang replies and the new, climbing B melody.
songs.development: Keeps the original C–A-flat–F-minor–G chord trajectory and opening riff. A newly composed eight-bar bridge takes over on charang over D-flat and E-flat colors; the guitar returns with higher answers and a longer cadence.

songs.title: Verdant Velocity
songs.description: Vibraphone carries the recognizable forest melody over nimble finger bass, crisp electric-piano chords and bright guitar pulses. Flute and congas answer the melody without slowing the groove.
songs.development: Preserves the B-Dorian hook and B-minor–E–A–D lift, but accelerates its gait. A new eight-bar flute melody moves through G, D, E and F-sharp dominant, then the vibes return with octave turns and marimba counter-rhythm.

songs.title: Chrome Heartbeat
songs.description: The boss riff now attacks on distortion guitar while power-kit backbeats and picked bass drive forward. Brass takes the new middle melody, with guitar interjections and crisp piano hits at the joins.
songs.development: Retains the F-minor repeated-note hook and its half-step G-flat threat. The eight-bar B section is a broad brass line over B-flat minor, D-flat, E-flat and C dominant; the last return extends the guitar hook upward.
instruments: Distortion guitar: short, forceful original boss motif
Brass section: new rising B-section tune and antiphonal stabs
Picked electric bass: octave and fifth drive
Bright piano and lean strings: punctuation and harmonic contour

songs.title: Glass Causeway - Prism Sprint
songs.description: Clean electric guitar plays the familiar climbing causeway tune over a skipping two-step kit and slap-bass line. Crystal synth answers flash between phrases; electric piano and muted guitar keep the offbeats moving.
songs.development: Quotes the A-minor hook and A-minor–F–C–G arc, with sharper gates and a new eight-bar rising bridge through D minor, E minor, F and G. A final E-dominant turn launches the stronger last statement.
instruments: Clean electric guitar: recognizably ascending Glass Causeway hook
Crystal synth: short glassy answers and a new bridge melody
Slap bass: syncopated fifths and octave pickups
Electric piano and muted guitar: separated two-step chord attacks

songs.title: Neon Market - Flash Sale
songs.description: Clavinet turns the market hook into a brisk, percussive riff. Slap bass and hand percussion power the four-on-the-floor groove, Hammond stabs fill the gaps and a tenor-sax middle section opens into brass replies.
songs.development: Keeps the D-Dorian melody and D-minor–G13–C–A-minor harmony. New sax-led B phrases move through F, C, G and A dominant before the original clav hook returns with higher brass answers.
instruments: Clavinet: original syncopated Dorian market melody

songs.title: Signal Garden - Sunburst
songs.style: Lydian piano-funk sprint with flute and alto-sax call and response
songs.description: The original upward garden hook starts on the first beat, now carried by a buoyant flute over bright syncopated piano, springy synth bass, guitar chops and conga flecks. A fresh alto-sax middle section answers in a lower, warmer register.
songs.development: 32 bars: A flute 1–8, new B sax 9–16, A with brass punctuation 17–24, a compact B answer 25–28 and a stronger A resolution 29–32. The source C–D–Em–G Lydian identity remains recognizable while bass, rhythm and B melody are rewritten.

songs.style: Brash synth-brass and FM-key trance/acid sprint
songs.description: Razor Bloom's angular C-minor hook lands immediately in bright synth brass, with a fast acid-like synth-bass figure, glassy FM keys and insistent electronic club percussion. The new B hook climbs into E-flat major before snapping through G7 back into the original riff.

songs.description: A full horn hook, octave-driving bass and racing strings arrive together. Razor Bloom's angular root/fifth/minor-third leap becomes a triumphant upward anthem; a new major-key violin B section opens the horizon before the largest horn return.

songs.description: A punchy trumpet hook answers a growling tenor sax while walking acoustic bass and swung ride cymbal keep the parade moving. Listen for the late upbeat brass kicks and the eight-bar dominant-chain bridge.
songs.development: New AABA32 form with an immediate eight-bar trumpet melody, an embellished second A, a contrasting tenor-led bridge and a final ensemble shout. Swing uses two-thirds-beat upbeats, not straight dance hats.

songs.title: Midnight Klezmer Express
songs.description: A curling clarinet melody leaps around the freygish flat-second and major-third color while accordion and tuba drive an exuberant two-beat dance. Violin replies and a brief accordion-led strain provide contrast.
songs.development: The first strain outlines D freygish with authored triplet turns. The B strain moves to G minor and lets accordion lead while clarinet answers. The final return adds violin countermelody and short ensemble cadences. This is a klezmer-inspired GM arrangement, not a claim of traditional performance authenticity.

songs.title: Circuit Raga
songs.description: A penetrating shanai-like reed hook and plucked sitar responses circle a D/A drone. Rapid conga/bongo patterns approximate contrasting tabla strokes; the B strain changes register and rhythmic grouping without turning into an ambient interlude.
songs.development: An original modal melody uses D–E♭–F♯–G–A–B♭–C♯ color over a mostly fixed tonic/fifth, with four-bar rhythmic cadences. The B strain gives sitar the lead and adds a flute answer. GM shanai, sitar and percussion are explicit instrumental approximations, not an authentic raga/tabla performance.

songs.title: Clockwork Gamelan
songs.description: Bright steel-pan and xylophone lines interlock over deep gong-like bells, wooden clicks and rolling toms. Listen for the answering pentatonic pattern that changes the accent grid halfway through. The gamelan influence is an interlocking idea rendered with GM approximations, not a claim of traditional instrumentation.
songs.development: A complete new percussion-led score: two complementary melodic streams, a contrasting higher pentatonic strain, and a denser final return. No dance backbeat, trap hats, four-on-the-floor kick, or sustained synth-pad bed.

instruments.role: Warm metallic principal phrase / steel-drum approximation

Bongos, toms, claves and triangle; no generic dance kit

songs.title: Cathedral Pinball
songs.description: A quick harpsichord subject ricochets into church-organ answers, bowed strings and a running cello. Listen for the bright major-side episode and the three-way return; timpani and orchestral percussion keep the first beat moving.
songs.development: An original two-bar contrapuntal subject receives a fifth-related answer, a contrasting G-major episode, and a compressed final development. Rhythmic life comes from rapid counterpoint and bass motion rather than a club beat.

songs.description: Muted-guitar upstrokes, a bright trumpet hook, trombone retorts and a picked bass barrel forward at 190 BPM. Listen for the guitar’s offbeats against the snare and the broader brass answer in the B strain.

songs.development: Original syncopated ragtime hooks, a contrasting E-flat-side episode, and alternating piano/calliope foregrounds create a fresh form. The rhythmic joke comes from grouped eighths and chromatic pickups rather than an unchanged dance template.

songs.title: Pixel Highlands
songs.description: Fiddle strains and a bagpipe answer race above nylon-guitar pulse, picked bass and a broad taiko/tom drive. Listen for the two distinct reel melodies, the little flute turns and the heavier octave return. The folk colors are General MIDI approximations.
songs.development: Two newly written reel-like strains alternate and develop over D-mixolydian and major-side harmony. Acoustic strumming, ornamented fiddle, bagpipe foreground changes and tom-led rock propulsion establish a different identity from the earlier electronic score.
